raw_response:
I am old now, 76, so I do not chase fancy things. I look first at what has worked on my own land. On the better plots I will still keep the wheat-maize rotation, because even if one side is weak, the other side can make up some income. Cotton I will keep on part of the land because I know how to manage it and it spreads risk. Chili I only keep on a small area because it needs more watching and more hand labor, but the price can be better if the year is smooth. With only two people in the house, I have to keep the plan steady and not make it too labor-heavy. I have a well, so if spring is dry I can save the crop, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate more than needed.

For wheat, I will put it on the main rotation land and sow in early October, about the same time as the village usually does. I usually put base fertilizer first, then one topdress around jointing if the stand looks good. I do not want to cut fertilizer too much, because if wheat turns yellow I lose yield fast. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant summer maize right away on the same land. That turnaround is always tight, so I will keep tillage simple, mostly straw handling and quick rotary work or direct planting if the machine is available. Cotton I will keep on a moderate area with enough fertilizer but not too much, and I will watch insects carefully because once aphids or bollworm get ahead, it becomes expensive. Chili I will keep on the smallest piece near the house where I can check it often. That crop brings cash, but it also needs more spraying and more hand work, so I will not expand it at my age.
